stories.title: N. Korea slams Japan's Yasukuni shrine visits as 'neo-militarist frenzy'
stories.summary: North Korea on Monday slammed Japanese politicians for visiting the controversial Yasukuni Shrine and sending ritual offerings, criticizing the move as "neo-militarist frenzy." The North issued the criticism in a commentary carried by the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA), accusing them of harboring militaristic ambitions by paying respects at the shrine on Aug. 15, the anniversary of Japan's 1945 surrender in World War II. The Yasukuni Shrine honors some 2.46 million Japanese war dead, including 14 Class. A criminals convicted by international tribunals for their roles in World War II. This year's visit carried even graver meaning, the KCNA said, coming alongside what it called Japan's "dangerous military moves that were unseen in past governments." It cited Japan's operational deployment of preemptive-strike weapons, revisions to its defense industry laws and attempts to revise nuclear-related legislation as evidence. Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's "surprise remote worship" revealed her "scheme to heighten the reinvasion mood" across the country and her efforts to "realize her long-cherished desire for overseas expansion," it said. "A neo-militarist frenzy whipped by Japan on the occasion of its defeat will bring a storm of destruction to the island nation," the KCNA said. The commentary was Pyongyang's latest denunciation of Tokyo amid a recent uptick in North Korea's criticism of what it describes as Japan's accelerating military buildup and efforts to revive its militaristic past.

stories.title: Six people injured in Nevada wildfire — agency
stories.summary: NEW YORK, August 24. At least six people were injured in a wildfire that broke out on August 22 near Reno, Nevada, the Associated Press reported. The fire dubbed Hawk spread across 53 square kilometers, according to the report. The flames destroyed several structures, and three emergency responders and three civilians were injured. Investigators believe the raging fire was caused by human activity, and an investigation is underway. Authorities have ordered 90,000 people to evacuate, with 42,000 local residents having been notified to leave their homes immediately.

stories.title: How easy is it to find an NHS dentist? It depends where you live
stories.summary: Hundreds of dentist practices are abandoning NHS work as the service drifts towards a two-tier system, new analysis suggests. Data analysed by the Nuffield Trust found that nearly 600 practices in England have withdrawn from NHS dentistry over the last 10 years. The decline has been particularly sharp in parts of the South West and East of England, raising concerns about growing inequalities in access to care. The analysis suggests more than one in 10 dental practices that once offered NHS care no longer do so, leaving it near impossible for some communities to find NHS appointments. NHS dental activity is 8% lower than it was pre Covid, while six in 10 adults have not seen an NHS dentist in two years. Of those who attempted to get a new appointment in the last two years, just 38% were successful, according to a Nuffield Trust Survey. Cornwall, Devon and Northamptonshire have seen some of the biggest reductions in the number of practices offering NHS care. In Cornwall, more than a quarter of practices that previously offered NHS treatment have stopped doing so, making it one of the starkest examples of the shift away from NHS dentistry. The findings come as ministers have pledged to tackle so-called "dental deserts", but dentists say the current deal is not viable. Many have handed back their NHS contracts because to work is loss-making. In Somerset, fewer than one in five dental practices now offers NHS services. Alan, 83, who lives in the county, says he has given up trying to find an NHS dentist.
